subject: website
name: Actual Budget
summary: A local-first budgeting app, built from upstream's open source (MIT) at a pinned commit, with upstream's own backend running in Orivon. Every script ships in its own files, with no analytics: Level 3. Not Level 4: by default it asks api.github.com for the newest release and fetches a news file from raw.githubusercontent.com, unverified connections the user did not start (both can be turned off). The budget stays on this computer; sync to a server the user names is optional. Not private: GitHub sees your IP address.

operations.name: Budget, record transactions, run reports
operations.note: The budget is a SQLite file in this app's own folder on this computer, with no account. Not private only because of the default GitHub requests.

operations.name: Import and export (CSV, budget zip)
operations.note: Files are read from and saved to folders the person picks; nothing is sent anywhere.

operations.name: Sync to a self-hosted Actual server
operations.note: Optional and off until the user enters a server address. The code does what it promises; the server holds the synced copy (encrypted if the user sets a password), sees your IP address and when you sync, and can withhold it.

connections.name: Update check (api.github.com)
connections.note: Made by default when a budget opens, unless the user turns the update notice off in Settings. It only decides whether a banner appears; the answer is not verified.

connections.name: News feed (raw.githubusercontent.com)
connections.note: A JSON file of announcements, fetched by default and cached for six hours, unless the user turns the news feed off in Settings. Its text is shown as received.

connections.name: Sync server chosen by the user
connections.note: Only the one address the user enters, over https. Bank connections, if the user sets any up, go through that server and are made by it.
